brief.subject: FTC moves to block vet supply deal; poor credit lifts car insurance
brief.headline: FTC Sues to Stop $3.5 Billion Vet Supply Merger; Poor-Credit Drivers Pay More
brief.dek: Regulators warn a vet distributor merger could raise pet care costs, while drivers with weak credit see sharply higher auto premiums.
brief.lede: The FTC sued today to block a $3.5 billion merger of the two largest veterinary supply distributors, warning it could raise prices for pet owners.

sections.heading: FTC Fights Vet Supply Megadeal
bullets: The FTC sued to block Covetrus from buying rival MWI Veterinary Supply for $3.5 billion.
Regulators say the pair are the two biggest distributors of veterinary products and services.
The agency argues the deal would push up costs for clinics, which could pass higher prices on to pet owners.
Covetrus owners Clayton, Dubilier & Rice and TPG are also named in the suit.

sections.heading: Weak Credit, Pricier Car Insurance
bullets: Drivers with poor credit saw auto premiums rise nearly 38% over the past three years, a 2026 rates report found.
Your credit standing can directly affect what you pay to insure a car, not just borrowing costs.
Households with damaged credit face a growing gap on a bill most drivers cannot skip.
